Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: nock-fleet[bot]
Message:
Helper templates: checks report their own failures; severity from real exit codes

Lint checks no longer discard stderr, and a failed check exits instead of
reading as a pass. The parse probe runs a copy of the policy with the audit
block neutralised under a throwaway HOME, with a timeout. vuln-scan picks one
verifier from the signing settings, tests for the trail before verifying, and
maps severity from the verifier's exit status (fresh install is setup, a
missing trail with prior evidence is HIGH, exit 2 on a present trail is
CRITICAL). Source line numbers in shipped templates are replaced with function
names, with a guard test.

Author: kkwills13
Message:
fix(approval): redact secret-shaped values under neutral keys (N8613) (#44)

summarizeValue previously only redacted on sensitive key-name match or >40 chars, so a short credential-shaped value under a neutral key (id/value/body) was forwarded to the Telegram approval prompt verbatim. Adds validate.LooksLikeSecret (reuses the CategorySecrets detectors) and applies it to every string + bare-numeric value regardless of key name, layered on the existing checks. Positive controls confirm harmless short scalars still render. go test/vet/gofmt clean.

Description: Discovered a GitHub OAuth Access Token, posing a risk of compromised GitHub account integrations and data leaks.
Author: kkwills13
Message:
ci: bring NockGuard review coverage up to sibling-product parity (claude-review + gitleaks) (#59)

* ci: add Claude code-review + gitleaks secret-scan to match sibling-product coverage

NockGuard had only ci.yml (build-test); sibling product NockLock runs a fuller review set.
Adds the two that fit a PUBLIC repo:
- claude-code-review.yml: Claude /code-review on every PR (app installed org-wide; NockLock
  uses this identical workflow; org secret CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN present).
- gitleaks.yml + .gitleaks-baseline.json: secret scanning on push + PR. Baseline pins the 13
  pre-existing history findings, all confirmed-safe fixtures (validate_test.go / summary_test.go
  test tokens, policy-lint.md doc examples, livedemo placeholder) so the scan is green and only
  flags NEW secrets. Verified locally: 'no leaks found' with the baseline.

Excludes NockLock's anvil.yml: its job condition is 'if: repository.private == true' and
NockGuard is public (gh api -> private:false), so it stays skipped here; it also mounts the
shared Codex credential on a self-hosted runner, widening the credential surface on a public repo.

* ci(gitleaks): pin download by sha256, least-priv permissions, no persisted creds

Addresses CodeRabbit Major finding on the secret-scan workflow:
- verify the gitleaks tarball against its SHA-256 (551f6fc8, independently confirmed
  against the live release asset) so a substituted download is rejected before extraction
- add explicit least-privilege 'permissions: contents: read'
- 'persist-credentials: false' on checkout (the scan never pushes)

Author: kkwills13
Message:
ci: bring NockGuard review coverage up to sibling-product parity (claude-review + gitleaks) (#59)

* ci: add Claude code-review + gitleaks secret-scan to match sibling-product coverage

NockGuard had only ci.yml (build-test); sibling product NockLock runs a fuller review set.
Adds the two that fit a PUBLIC repo:
- claude-code-review.yml: Claude /code-review on every PR (app installed org-wide; NockLock
  uses this identical workflow; org secret CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN present).
- gitleaks.yml + .gitleaks-baseline.json: secret scanning on push + PR. Baseline pins the 13
  pre-existing history findings, all confirmed-safe fixtures (validate_test.go / summary_test.go
  test tokens, policy-lint.md doc examples, livedemo placeholder) so the scan is green and only
  flags NEW secrets. Verified locally: 'no leaks found' with the baseline.

Excludes NockLock's anvil.yml: its job condition is 'if: repository.private == true' and
NockGuard is public (gh api -> private:false), so it stays skipped here; it also mounts the
shared Codex credential on a self-hosted runner, widening the credential surface on a public repo.

* ci(gitleaks): pin download by sha256, least-priv permissions, no persisted creds

Addresses CodeRabbit Major finding on the secret-scan workflow:
- verify the gitleaks tarball against its SHA-256 (551f6fc8, independently confirmed
  against the live release asset) so a substituted download is rejected before extraction
- add explicit least-privilege 'permissions: contents: read'
- 'persist-credentials: false' on checkout (the scan never pushes)

Message:
feat(skills): beginner security skills — /threat-model, /vuln-scan, /policy-lint (N7997) (#20)

Add three Claude Code slash commands for beginner-facing NockGuard security guidance:

- /threat-model: guided session from blank slate to a policy matching the real risk surface
- /vuln-scan: scan policy file + audit trail for gaps, ranked CRITICAL-LOW with concrete fixes
- /policy-lint: structural/logic lint before deploy — catches implicit allow-alls, bare wildcards,
  rate_limit missing window, unresolved env vars, and unknown keys

Skills live at .claude/commands/ (repo-level, for NockGuard contributors) and
templates/warden/.claude/commands/ (bundled with the Warden agent template for deployers).
Updated warden README with deployment instructions and a skill reference table.

Manual run verified all checks fire correctly against livedemo/policy.yaml (clean pass)
and a synthetic bad-policy fixture (all error/warning paths triggered).

Author: kkwills13
Message:
feat(approval): show redacted params in the approval prompt (#13)

The Phase 5 human-approval prompt showed only Agent + Tool — req.Params was
passed but never rendered (telegram.go:57). A human approving a spend or
kill_switch couldn't see the amount or target: they approved an action they
couldn't see. You can't claim 'accountable' if the human consents blind.

Add summarizeParams: a redacted, length-capped summary of the tool-call params
for the prompt. Conservative by design — shows consent-relevant scalars
(amounts, targets, short strings, bools) verbatim, redacts sensitive-looking
keys (secret/token/key/password/auth/...), redacts long values (likely
secrets/blobs) keeping only their length, shows nested objects/arrays as typed
placeholders (never recurses into them), and summarizes a non-object by size
only. Raw params are still never sent to Telegram (nor written to the audit
trail).

Audit finding NockGuard 1d#11 (top-5 adjacent — the 'approve blind' credibility
gap on the accountable claim).

Tests cover: spend amount + kill-switch target shown; sensitive keys and long
values redacted (with explicit no-leak assertions); nested not recursed;
non-object size-only; empty/absent; length cap. go test ./... -race green;
gofmt + vet clean.
